sample_unit: patients tested for amyloidosis after AI flag (of 256 eligible)

links.outcome: Model discrimination across racial/ethnic subgroups (Hispanic, non-Hispanic Black, non-Hispanic White)
links.effect: AUROC 0.85 internal and 0.82 (95% CI 0.81-0.83) external, with similar performance across Hispanic, non-Hispanic Black, and non-Hispanic White patients.
links.quote: It had good discrimination for ATTR-CM detection with an area under the receiver operator characteristic curve of 0.85 (5-fold cross-validation, 0.77-0.85) in the internal set and 0.82 (95% CI, .81-0.83) in the external test set with similar performance in Hispanic, non-Hispanic Black, and non-Hispanic White patients.

links.outcome: ATTR-CM testing positivity and new diagnoses versus historical and contemporary controls
links.effect: 24/50 (48%) diagnosed; positivity more than 2.8 times historical controls (15.3%); 18% relative increase in new diagnoses vs prior year; patient outcomes not shown to improve.
links.quote: The positivity rate was more than 2.8 times higher than historical controls (15.3%; 95% CI, 13.1%-17.9%; P < .001), with an 18% relative increase in new diagnoses vs the prior year.

links.outcome: Model performance on external test set from a different academic site
links.effect: Internal AUROC 0.85 (5-fold CV 0.77-0.85) versus external test set AUROC 0.82 (95% CI 0.81-0.83) in 422 patients.
links.quote: The model was trained and validated at a large academic referral site for ATTR-CM with external validation at an academic site.

unlisted_practices: Using AI screening to identify patients for targeted diagnostic testing of underdiagnosed disease with physician approval before patient outreach

screen.reason: Prospective clinical trial evaluating the real-world deployment and diagnostic yield of an AI-augmented screening system (ATTRACTnet) for ATTR-CM, but it does not compare specific deployment practices/safeguards head-to-head.
